description:
PearTune plays the music library on a machine you own - an Umbrel, a NAS, an old desktop, a laptop - from anywhere, over a direct encrypted connection between your phone and that machine.

  No port forwarding, no VPN, no dynamic DNS, no account, and no copy of your library in anyone's cloud. The music never leaves your hardware: it streams through the live connection while it plays.

  PLEASE READ FIRST

PearTune needs that machine running the free PearTune host, which is the source of the music. It is not a player for files stored on your phone. If you do not have a server yet, setup offers "I don't have one yet", which plays a small built-in demo library so you can look around before you have a library to connect to.

  READS THE LIBRARY YOU ALREADY HAVE

  Point the host at a music server you already run and PearTune uses its library, its artwork and its transcoding. It speaks the Subsonic API, so Navidrome, Gonic, LMS, Ampache, Funkwhale, Koel, Nextcloud Music, Supysonic and Airsonic all work, and it reads Jellyfin and Emby servers directly. Point it at a plain folder of files instead and PearTune reads the tags itself - artist, album, track number, year and embedded cover art - so a folder is a real library, not a list of filenames.

  IN THE APP
  
  - Browse by artist, album, genre or track, with artwork
  - Search the whole library
  - Gapless playback, shuffle and repeat, a sleep timer
  - Background and lock screen audio
  - Playlists you make on your phone, plus the read-only ones your server already has
  - Favourites and resume points that follow you between your own devices
  - Playback hands over rather than doubling up - start on one device and the other pauses
  - Downloads: pin an album to keep it on the phone, for a flight or a tunnel
  - Ask the owner for music you cannot find, and see what they did with it

  THE LIBRARY DOES NOT HAVE TO BE YOURS

  Someone can let a friend or a family member in, each as their own person with their own devices, their own favourites and their own resume points, and no login to pass around. The owner sees every device and can revoke one, or everything one person holds, in a second - mid-song, not on next login. Nobody who is let in ever receives a copy of a file.

  PAIRING IS ONE SCAN

  Scan a QR code and you are in. There is no password, no server address and no account to create. The connection itself proves which device is calling, so there is no token to leak, copy or forget to rotate.

  WHEN A DIRECT CONNECTION IS NOT POSSIBLE
  
  Some mobile networks and locked-down wifi refuse a direct connection between two devices. When that happens PearTune can fall back to a relay run by PeerLoom, which forwards encrypted data it cannot read and keeps no copy of it. Your phone always tries a direct connection first, PearTune asks before streaming a library's music through the relay, and one switch in Settings turns it off entirely.

  OPEN SOURCE

PearTune is MIT licensed and developed in the open. The host you run on your own machine is free, and so is the app.
promotionalText: The music on a machine you own, playable anywhere. No port forwarding, no VPN, no account, and no copy of your library in anyone's cloud.
whatsNew:
New Features
  - Like the song you're listening to straight from the player. The heart is on the player itself now, in both looks.

  Improvements                                                                                                                                         
  - The albums grid keeps loading as you scroll. No more "Load more" button.
  - Uses less memory while playing. The app now fetches music a little at a time instead of pulling a whole song ahead.
                                                                                                                                                       
  Bug Fixes
  - Music now pauses when your Bluetooth car or headset disconnects, or when you unplug wired headphones, instead of sometimes carrying on through the phone's speaker.
  - Your queue no longer disappears after a pause. If the connection to your library drops while the phone is locked, the queue is kept and comes back as soon as the library is reachable again.
  - Tapping Shuffle on an artist now really shuffles from the first song, so the list no longer runs out after a few tracks.
  - WMA files from a Jellyfin library now play, the same as from a folder library. (Needs the updated library host.)
  - Music folders that use shortcuts or symbolic links are now included in your library. (Needs the updated library host.)
  - On a Mac, "Update now" works again. Note for Mac users already on 1.0.2 or 1.0.3: install this version by hand once, and updates will apply themselves from then on.
